title: Mastering variation: variance components and personalised medicine

cost.compute_notes: JATS full text from Europe PMC, rendered with tools/jats2txt.py to 46,912 characters. The simulation appendix was transcribed and re-run inside mccutcheon2022-reappraising-variability/reanalysis/m10_senn_identity.py; no separate reanalysis folder, because the code belongs next to the argument it serves.

triggers: can a parallel group trial detect individual differences in treatment response
what design is needed to identify patient-by-treatment interaction
components of variation in a clinical trial
is there a personal element in response to treatment
n-of-1 trials and repeated period crossover designs
why is a responder rate not a real quantity
does increased variance in the treated arm prove heterogeneity
replication is the key to studying interaction
additive scale transformation and clinical relevance of interaction

claims.statement: Identification of differential response to treatment requires replication at the level at which differential response is claimed. A parallel-group trial identifies only the between-treatment component; between-patient variation, patient-by-treatment interaction and within-patient occasion-to-occasion variation are confounded in its error term.
claims.scope: Senn's Tables 1 and 2. Four components: A between treatments, B between patients, C patient-by-treatment interaction, D within patients. C is the quantity personalised medicine is about, and is sigma_TE^2 in the variability-ratio literature's notation.

quantities.name: components_identifiable_parallel_group
quantities.unit: fraction of the four components A,B,C,D
quantities.source: Senn 2016 Table 2: parallel group identifies A; error term is B + C + D

quantities.name: components_identifiable_classical_crossover
quantities.source: Senn 2016 Table 2: identifies A and B; error term is C + D

quantities.name: components_identifiable_repeated_period_crossover
quantities.source: Senn 2016 Table 2: identifies A, B and C; error term is D. The only design in the table that identifies C.

our_assessment.why: This is the result the whole psychiatric variability-ratio literature is trying to get around, and it was in print in 2015. It is a design fact, not a modelling opinion: interaction is separable from error only when the treatments are replicated within the units across which the interaction is claimed, which for individual response means the patient. Everything I established empirically in mccutcheon2022-reappraising-variability is a special case or a demonstration of it. PRIORITY IS SENN'S and should be cited as such.

claims.statement: An increased variance in the experimental arm can equally reflect patient-by-treatment interaction or occasion-to-occasion variation that is larger under one treatment than the other, so the variability ratio cannot distinguish real individual response from heteroscedastic noise.
claims.scope: Senn's own counter-example: an oral versus intravenous formulation, where absorption may vary between patients (component C) or from occasion to occasion within a patient (component D).

our_assessment.why: A fourth axis of non-identification for the variability ratio, and the one I had not articulated before reading this. The other three now on record in areas/treatment-effect-heterogeneity.md are: additive versus multiplicative homogeneity (which statistic tests which null); VR bounding rather than measuring heterogeneity (two arms with the same two moments are consistent with a uniform effect and with a mixture); and rho, the correlation between individual effect and control outcome. This one is different in kind from all three: it is not about the estimator but about what a larger variance can physically MEAN. No amount of statistical care removes it, because it is a design limitation.

claims.statement: Two worlds with identical marginal distributions of the observed treatment difference can differ several-fold in the real, repeatable component of individual response; only a replicate period distinguishes them.
claims.scope: Senn's Figures 2 and 3, double cross-over (his Table 3 sequences), 1000 patients, differences active minus placebo with mean 0.5 L FEV1 and variance 0.04 L^2, test-retest correlation across replicate period-pairs of 0.90 and 0.02.

quantities.name: sigma_C_high_reliability_world_simulated
quantities.source: maria 2026, m10 in the mccutcheon folder: his appendix parameters re-run; observed replicate correlation 0.9030; analytic value 0.1897

quantities.name: sigma_C_low_reliability_world_simulated
quantities.source: maria 2026, m10: observed replicate correlation 0.0440; analytic value 0.0283

quantities.name: marginal_sd_of_observed_difference_both_worlds
quantities.source: maria 2026, m10: 0.1928 and 0.1968 respectively; the two worlds are indistinguishable to any design that observes one difference per patient

quantities.name: ratio_analytic_versus_simulated_sigma_C_contrast
quantities.source: maria 2026, m10: analytic 0.1897/0.0283 = 6.7 against simulated 0.183/0.041 = 4.4. The gap is sampling noise in the estimated replicate correlation at n = 1000.

our_assessment.why: Reproduced from the parameters in his appendix, which are stated precisely enough to re-run seven years later with no data deposit at all -- worth recording against the assumption that reproducibility requires a repository. I got it wrong the first time and record that here rather than silently: I read the figures as pairs of (placebo, active) OUTCOMES correlated r and implemented that. They are pairs of DIFFERENCES across two replicate period-pairs, so r is the test-retest reliability of a patient's own effect. The correction made his point STRONGER than my misreading did, because in the correct version both worlds also have identical marginals, so a classical cross-over is fooled too and not only a parallel-group trial. The 6.7 versus 4.4 gap is the honest price of the only design that identifies the quantity: even a double cross-over in 1,000 patients pins sigma_C down loosely.

claims.statement: Provided the response distributions under two treatments do not cross as a covariate varies, a transformation exists making the treatment difference constant, so the presence or absence of statistical interaction is partly a choice of scale rather than a fact about the treatment.
claims.scope: Senn following Berrington de Gonzalez and Cox. Argued, not derived here.

our_assessment.why: Accepted as stated, and it explains a result of mine that had no explanation. On 2026-09-02 I built a diagnostic that asks whether a corpus supports ADDITIVE or MULTIPLICATIVE homogeneity, and both corpora tested came back additive. I recorded that as an empirical finding about antidepressants and mindfulness. Senn's point is that the existence of a scale on which the effect is additive is close to generic, so 'the corpus chooses additive' is weaker evidence about the treatment than I took it to be -- it is partly evidence that the outcome scale was already a reasonable one. NARROWER SCOPE because the converse still bites: a qualitative interaction that reverses the sign for some patients cannot be transformed away, and my diagnostic would not detect one. What survives from my 09-02 work is the operational half -- lnVR and lnCVR test different nulls, the choice is load-bearing, and no paper states which was made.

claims.statement: Published non-responder rates by disease (38% depression, 48% migraine, 52% osteoporosis, 75% cancer) trace to a single secondary source and cannot be checked.
claims.scope: An FDA report citing Spear et al., whose stated source is the 54th edition of the Physicians' Desk Reference.

our_assessment.why: I have not gone back to the FDA report or to Spear et al., so this is recorded at the depth I actually read it: Senn's characterisation, not my check of it. It matters because these numbers circulate widely as the empirical basis for personalised medicine, and if the provenance is as he describes then a large policy literature rests on a table with no method attached. Marked for checking rather than quoted.

checked.result: USABLE, and better than a PDF for this paper: Tables 1, 2 and 3 render as cells, and Tables 1-2 ARE the argument. 46,912 characters. The figures are images and are not extracted, but the appendix states their generating parameters in words, which is what made the reproduction possible.

Section 1 re-runs his Figures 2-3 from the appendix parameters. Deliberately housed with the mccutcheon record rather than here: it exists to serve that argument, and splitting it would give two half-scripts and one broken import.

relations.why: Not by name -- the paper predates it -- but the design argument applies directly: that analysis reads component C off a parallel-group trial, which Senn's Table 2 says cannot be done.
Likewise. McCutcheon et al. cite the adjacent Senn 2018 Nature piece and adopt none of the identification argument.

My additive-versus-multiplicative diagnostic returned 'additive' on both corpora. Senn's scale argument says a transformation to additivity nearly always exists, so that verdict is weaker evidence about the treatment than I recorded, and stronger evidence that the outcome scale was already reasonable.
The mindfulness corpus is parallel-group throughout and inherits the same confounding of B, C and D.

open_questions: Senn cites Senn, Rolfe and Julious on a repeated cross-over in Parkinsonism as an example where individual response WAS identified. That is the one design in this whole area that answers the question, and I have not read it. If it reports a test-retest correlation of individual effects it is the only empirical anchor available for the psychiatric debate.

Kalow et al. proposed cross-over trials as the trialist's equivalent of the twin study. Unread, and it is the conceptual bridge between the heritability literature (which routinely separates components) and the trial literature (which routinely does not).

Marwick et al. 2018 systematically reviewed n-of-1 trials in schizophrenia. If any used replicated periods, sigma_C is directly estimable for antipsychotics and the entire McCutcheon-Munkholm dispute has an empirical answer nobody has looked up.
c5 is recorded unverified: the FDA non-responder table and its provenance through Spear et al. to the Physicians' Desk Reference has not been checked by me.
